item.title: The long-deployed USS Lincoln returns home to San Diego Bay
item.description: The USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier has returned home after a record-setting uninterrupted time at sea supporting the Iran war. The extended deployment drew attention following reports of crew stress and supply shortages.
item.content:encoded:

(Image credit: Gregory Bull)

item.title: New U.S. indictment charges former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro with torture
item.description: U.S. authorities added new torture charges to their case against former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro, ramping up pressure on the ousted authoritarian leader already fighting drug trafficking allegations.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: South Korea to recall its ambassador to Ukraine over North Korean POW dispute
item.description: The South Korean announcement on Thursday came days after its President Lee Jae Myung threatened unspecified punitive steps if Ukraine refuses to apologize over the revelation.

item.title: South Korea test-flies its first domestically developed hypersonic weapon
item.description: The test follows North Korea's recent hypersonic missile test. Tensions between the Koreas have increased after land mine explosions injured three South Korean soldiers near the border. North Korea denies responsibility.

item.title: Isaias intensifies to hurricane. And, judge orders Pike execution evidence preserved
item.description: People in the Gulf are preparing for bad weather this weekend after Isaias intensified into a hurricane. And, a judge has ordered Christa Pike's failed execution evidence be preserved.

item.title: Syrian general accused of atrocities is protected by U.S. and Lebanon, NPR and BBC find
item.description: A former Syrian general wanted for crimes against humanity is living quietly in Lebanon, bankrolled and protected by American and Lebanese authorities, a BBC/NPR investigation has found.

item.title: Former ambassador on NATO's meeting in Ukraine and the ongoing war
item.description: Military representatives from all 32 NATO member states met in Kyiv. NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with Kurt Volker, former U.S. ambassador to NATO, about the meeting and the ongoing war.

item.title: Maricarmen, the 87-year-old woman whose eviction shook Spain, has died
item.description: María del Carmen Abascal, the 87-year-old woman whose eviction from her Madrid home sparked nationwide protests across Spain and unleashed a political crisis, died on Wednesday while hospitalized.
